title: Real and Virtual Images
notes: **Real image:** formed when reflected rays actually converge at a point. Can be projected onto a screen. Formed by concave mirrors when the object is beyond the focal point.

**Virtual image:** formed when reflected rays only appear to diverge from a point behind the mirror. Cannot be projected. Formed by convex mirrors and by concave mirrors when the object is inside the focal length.
**Concave mirror:** converges rays. Object beyond C gives real inverted diminished image; between C and F gives real inverted magnified image; inside F gives virtual upright magnified image.
**Convex mirror:** diverges rays. Always forms virtual upright diminished image regardless of object position. Field of view is wider, useful for rear-view mirrors.
**Plane mirror:** forms virtual upright same-size image at the same distance behind the mirror as the object is in front.
